single_session.description:
Send `true`. Links every event in the batch to the session named by
each event's `session_id`.

Channel.description: Identifies the integration type. Server-to-server callers send `s2s`.

event_type.description:
What happened. `impression`, `viewed`, and `signal_response` are
expected from every server-to-server integration; send `dismissal`
as well if your UI lets a customer close an offer:

- `impression` — the element rendered and is visible to the customer.
  Send one for each element that renders. If you delay appearance,
  raise it when the element is unhidden.
- `viewed` — the creative was at least 50% visible for one continuous
  second, matching the [IAB](https://www.iab.com/) viewability
  definition. Exclude bot traffic and any other invalid activity.
  Send one for each creative that becomes viewable.
- `signal_response` — the customer engaged with a response option.
  Send one for each interaction.
- `dismissal` — the customer dismissed the offer without engaging
  with a response option, for example by closing it. Send one per
  dismissed element.

instance_id.description:
A UUID you generate for this event, used to deduplicate retries. Send
the same value if you resend the same event.

timestamp.description: When the event occurred, in Unix epoch milliseconds.

parent_id.description:
The `instance_guid` of the element this event is about, taken from the
offers response — the creative's for an impression, a response
option's for a response.

Echo the value verbatim. It may carry a type prefix such as
`ad:<uuid>`; send it exactly as returned.

token.description:
The event token for that element, from the offers response. Each
element carries its own token — send the one belonging to the element
named by `parent_id`.

capture_method.description: How the event was captured, e.g. `ClientProvided`.
